title: Binance Reports $6.3 Billion Breach, Freezes $3 Billion in Largest Crypto Heist
text: Binance Reports $6.3 Billion Breach, Freezes $3 Billion in Largest Crypto Heist Binance disclosed a $6.3 billion security breach, the largest crypto heist ever, freezing about $3 billion as markets fell and stablecoin issuers froze over $2.5 billion. Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a security breach caused an estimated $6.3 billion impact, which analysts called possibly the biggest crypto heist ever. The exchange has frozen about $3 billion of affected assets and said it would cover all hacking losses. Binance said an initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of its engineers. That access let an attacker reach one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals. It gave no update on the remaining $3.3 billion.Markets React to Binance BreachMarkets reacted immediately in early Asian trading on Friday, October 30. Bitcoin dropped more than 3% to a six-week low of $76,368. Ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko.Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8%, while bitcoin buyer Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading. The incident could be the world's biggest crypto heist, according to analytics firm Chainalysis and other industry experts. It's the biggest hack in history, said Aravind Srinivasan, head of large crypto market maker GSR's systematic OTC business.Analysts said the breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure from higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers. Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group in Hong Kong, said it may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralized exchanges, as well as counterparty, solvency and liquidity risks.Binance Freezes Deposits and WithdrawalsBinance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally. It had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report. User funds remain safe, Binance said in a statement. As a precaution, all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while our security teams conduct checks, secure wallet infrastructure, and trace affected assets, with the close support of our law enforcement and industry partners.Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches, according to its website. Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident. Circle froze more than $800 million.World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said on Thursday it worked with cryptocurrency custodian BitGo to freeze funds stolen in what it described as a Binance hack. Binance co-founder Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen. Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said.Ripple and Tether Freeze Linked AssetsJack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple, said the company was closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance. He said Ripple was freezing affected funds and coordinating with relevant parties. Miguel Morel, CEO of blockchain intelligence firm Arkham, said data indicated that billions of dollars appeared to have been hacked from Binance by an unknown actor. The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts.Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry's vulnerability to hackers. Authorities have warned that organized crime groups are increasingly using cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside the traditional financial system. Binance.US, a separate cryptocurrency exchange, said it was not affected by the security incident. Coinbase said it was unaffected and was monitoring the situation. In an unrelated incident earlier on Thursday, prediction market operator Polymarket temporarily halted trading after a security incident involving a third-party provider. It later resumed trading and said it would fully reimburse affected traders.It's becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them, said Bernardo Brites, CEO of Trace Finance, a payments and stablecoin infrastructure company. My view is that users will move away from smaller and medium-sized exchanges, becoming too risky to park your money somewhere that couldn't cover a hack of meaningful size.
